sector: Industrial IoT / Commercial Refrigeration Hardware & SaaS
overview: AoFrio Limited (formerly Wellington Drive Technologies, founded 1986, renamed September 2022) is a New Zealand-headquartered, NZX-listed hardware-enabled SaaS company that designs and manufactures energy-efficient electronically commutated (EC) motors and fans, and IoT-enabled smart controllers/cloud connectivity (SCS Connect, SCS 800, AoFrio iQ) for commercial refrigeration in the food and beverage industry, principally bottle coolers used by Coca-Cola system bottlers, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo and other global beverage brands. Note: this is a genuine confirmation, not an assumption carried over from the prior report -- the FY2010-FY2025 annual reports and the FY2026 interim/quarterly filings in research/AOF.NZ/Extracted/ are consistently Wellington Drive Technologies/AoFrio filings (motors, fans, IoT, refrigeration); there is no forestry business, Augusta-branded fund, or NZ forestry context anywhere in the filings under this ticker. The company reports two segments, Motors and IoT, sells globally with heavy revenue concentration in the Americas, and is mid-transition from a hardware-led business toward a hardware-enabled, AI-powered SaaS model -- a transition now visibly straining 2026 results as the legacy Motors business shrinks faster than the new SCS 800/AoFrio iQ SaaS platform can yet replace it.

business_model.summary: Revenue splits between hardware sales of EC motors/fans (commoditized, lower margin, largely transactional) and IoT hardware plus recurring multi-year cloud data/software connection fees (higher margin, increasingly recurring). FY25 (year ended 31-Dec-2025) revenue was a record NZ$83.2m (+4.4% YoY): IoT NZ$47.1m (+8.9%, 42.5% gross margin) and Motors NZ$36.1m (flat, 17.7% gross margin). FY2026 has since deteriorated materially: 9 months to 30-Sep-2026 revenue was $50.3m, down 20% (-$12.6m) YoY, as Motors revenue fell 43.7% to $16.5m (gross profit nearly halved to $3.3m from $5.5m) while IoT revenue was roughly flat at $33.8m (+$0.2m); 9M26 EBITDA was $0.8m versus $2.7m in the prior-year period, though gross margin improved to 34.4% (from 31.3%) purely on mix-shift toward higher-margin IoT. Management's FY26 guidance, given with the 29-October-2026 3Q26 update, is for full-year revenue of ~$73m (~$10m below FY25) and EBITDA of ~$3m -- a guide that has now been lowered twice during 2026 (from 'expected improvement' at FY25 results in Feb-2026, to 'broadly consistent with FY25' at the 1H26 result in Aug-2026, to the current ~$10m-lower figure). Recurring SaaS/cellular data revenue remains small: cellular (SCS 800 + Gateway) revenue was $3.2m in 9M26, about 9.5% of IoT revenue, against a long-term company target of 50% of group revenue being recurring; $18.6m of invoiced revenue was deferred on the balance sheet at 30-June-2026 (30-June-2025: $16.8m), to be recognized over 1-10 year contracts as the installed base of connected devices (3.68m at 30-June-2026, +15% YoY) converts to recognized revenue.

revenue_streams.name: IoT (hardware + connectivity/SaaS)
revenue_streams.trend: flat to modestly growing in 2026 (9M26 +0.6% YoY) while Motors collapses, so its revenue share keeps rising

revenue_streams.name: Motors and Fans
revenue_streams.trend: declining sharply (9M26 -43.7% YoY) on the lost largest US motor customer plus other customers shifting to lower-spec, lower-cost motors

revenue_streams.name: Cellular/recurring SaaS revenue (subset of IoT, recognized)
revenue_streams.trend: growing off a small base ($3.2m of 9M26 revenue); management expects cellular revenue to rise significantly in 2027 as SCS 800/iQ trials convert to commercial orders

business_model.customer_type: B2B - enterprise, historically concentrated among global beverage bottlers/brands (Coca-Cola system bottlers, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo), OEMs, and USA appliance/water-heater manufacturers; FY25 saw four customers each individually >=10% of revenue together account for 49% of Group revenue ($40.5m of $83.2m), all within the Americas segment (up from two customers/27% in FY24). The concentration risk has since crystallized and broadened: not only has the single largest USA motor customer been lost (onshoring supply to avoid tariffs), but during 2Q/3Q26 other motor customers also shifted toward lower-specification, lower-cost motors, indicating the pressure is not confined to one account. Partially offsetting this, AoFrio won its first SCS 800/AoFrio iQ purchase orders from major US bottlers in 3Q26, and over 30 customers have been onboarded to AoFrio iQ through early pilots.
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~85% (LATAM plus USA) in FY25, APAC 8.3%, EMEA 7.0%; North America previously a growth driver via ECR2 motors into water heaters/supermarket display units and early SCS IoT launch, now the source of the 2026 Motors downturn; South America (core CDE/LATAM base) revenue declined 12.5% YoY in FY25 on reduced demand. A new Food Retail growth vector is emerging in Latin America: a 70-store rollout with a major Latin American supermarket chain is progressing in 2026, with the customer discussing further store additions.

main_competitors: Generic/local EC motor and fan manufacturers (especially in EMEA and now in Americas on price)
In-house/legacy telemetry and asset-tracking vendors for cooler fleets
Traditional AC-motor incumbents being displaced by EC technology
competitive_position.market_position: Long-established (40-year, founded 1986 as Wellington Drive Technologies), high-share incumbent supplier of EC motors/fans and connected controllers to the global cold drink equipment (CDE)/bottle cooler market, particularly strong in LATAM; a much smaller, earlier-stage challenger in IoT-enabled fleet SaaS platforms versus larger industrial IoT and cold-chain software players. 3.68 million coolers now connected to the AoFrio cloud (as of the November 2026 40th-anniversary announcement), up from 3.2 million at FY25 year-end.

moat_factors.description: SCS/Monitor/Click/SCS 800 devices installed on coolers create a base of 3.68m connected devices (+15% YoY) and long-dated (1-10 year) data contracts ($18.6m deferred revenue at 30-Jun-2026), generating switching costs once fleets are connected and integrated into customer operations

Decades-long relationships with global beverage brands and bottlers (Coca-Cola system, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo) and high customer NPS (+62 in FY25) support renewal and cross-sell, and translated into AoFrio's first SCS 800/AoFrio iQ purchase orders from major US bottlers in 3Q26 -- though this coexists with severe customer concentration risk that has now materialized and broadened across the Motors customer base

ECR2 motor technology delivers validated energy savings (up to 68% in bundled configurations) that align with customer ESG targets and evolving efficiency regulations (e.g., US DOE water heater standards), supporting product pull-through

Growing connected fleet (3.68m devices) improves AoFrio iQ's fleet insights; SCS 800 and the general-release AoFrio iQ SaaS platform were commercially launched in June 2026, over 30 customers have been onboarded to iQ via early pilots, and an AI-enabled 'Ask iQ' fleet-insights feature launched in October 2026. First commercial purchase orders landed in 3Q26, but cellular/recurring revenue is still only ~6% of group revenue and the platform remains early-stage at commercial scale

Micro-cap scale (market cap roughly NZ$30m as of October 2026, down from a 52-week high near NZ$0.11/share to ~NZ$0.05/share) limits R&D budget, negotiating leverage and resilience versus larger diversified industrial competitors; the stock has materially de-rated through 2026 as guidance was repeatedly lowered

weaknesses: Motors segment is a commoditized, price-competitive, low-margin business (17.7% FY25, deteriorating further as mix and pricing pressure bite) exposed to aggressive competitor pricing and tariff-driven customer reshoring; this has broadened in 2026 from a single lost customer into a wider shift by other motor customers toward lower-specification, lower-cost products, driving a 43.7% 9-month Motors revenue decline

Customer concentration risk has crystallized and is spreading: the single largest USA motor customer sourced elsewhere in 2026 due to tariffs, and other motor customers followed with lower-spec substitution; four customers = 49% of FY25 revenue, all in the Americas

Recurring/SaaS (cellular) revenue is still a small share of the business (~6% of 9M26 group revenue, ~9.5% of IoT revenue) relative to the long-stated 50% target; AoFrio iQ and SCS 800 only reached commercial launch in mid-2026 and purchase orders only began converting in 3Q26

Continued statutory losses (1H26 loss $2.1m, worse than 1H25's $1.8m loss) even as EBITDA improved modestly, aided by a one-off $1.2m RDTI tax credit in 1H26; FY26 EBITDA guidance of ~$3m is below FY25's $3.5m, and revenue guidance has been cut twice during 2026 (record FY25 to an expected ~12% FY26 decline)

growth_drivers: First commercial purchase orders for SCS 800 and AoFrio iQ secured from major US bottlers in 3Q26, following commercial launch in June 2026 and 33 global customer trials; management expects cellular revenue to rise significantly in 2027 as proof-of-concept trials convert to commercial orders, targeting a combined ~700,000-unit/year US/Europe cellular controller TAM
AI-enabled 'Ask iQ' fleet-insights feature launched October 2026, extending the AoFrio iQ platform and intended to differentiate the SaaS offering and drive annual recurring revenue growth

Food Retail vertical progressing with a 70-store rollout for a major Latin American supermarket chain, with the customer discussing further store additions; management plans to invest in customer-facing sales staff in 2H26 to drive 2027+ diversification revenue

Motors margin-protection initiatives: lower-cost component sourcing for the existing motor specification and development of a new lower-cost motor, both expected to take effect in early 2027, aimed at slowing the segment's share loss to cheaper competitor products

Two-path FY26-FY30 growth strategy (December 2025 Investor Day) remains the stated framework: self-funded path (~10% revenue CAGR to ~$140m/EBITDA $14m by FY30) versus a Board-preferred, externally-capitalized 'aspirational' path (>3x revenue to $300m, EBITDA $50m by FY30); $8.9m of a $15m capital-raise target was raised via a May 2026 placement and June 2026 rights issue, with deployment toward CDE growth beginning in 2H26 after first being used to pay down debt
Material net-debt reduction in 1H26 (net bank debt fell to $5.1m at 30-Jun-2026 from $8.2m at 31-Dec-2025) improves balance-sheet capacity to fund the growth plan without immediate further dilution

Secular tailwind from cold-chain energy efficiency, refrigerant/ESG regulation, and increasing enterprise appetite for connected/AI-driven asset management across cooler fleets; 40-year operating history (marked in a November 2026 anniversary announcement) and 3.68m connected coolers underscore installed-base scale

business.risk: Customer concentration and Motors commoditization spreading beyond one account
business.description: AoFrio's largest USA motor customer has been lost (onshoring to avoid tariffs), and during 2Q/3Q26 other motor customers also shifted to lower-specification, lower-cost motors -- showing the pressure is systemic to the Motors segment, not an isolated event. Motors revenue fell 43.7% over 9M26 and FY26 group revenue guidance has been cut from FY25's $83.2m record to ~$73m

business.risk: Execution risk on new product/SaaS launches and the Motors cost-reduction response
business.description: Growth thesis depends on SCS 800/AoFrio iQ converting recent first purchase orders (3Q26) into material 2027 recurring revenue, and on a new lower-cost motor (targeted early 2027) restoring Motors competitiveness; both are unproven at scale as of November 2026

business.risk: Product obsolescence / long sales and qualification cycles
business.description: OEM/bottler capital purchase cycles are multi-year; new hardware must pass customer qualification programmes, slowing revenue realization from new launches

Management flagged in the 3Q26 update that Q4 demand is inherently harder to forecast because bottlers and OEM suppliers typically finalise cooler budgets late in the year, adding uncertainty to the ~$73m FY26 guide

financial.description: Company has posted statutory net losses in recent periods (1H26 loss $2.1m, worse than 1H25's $1.8m loss; FY25 loss $2.1m, FY24 loss $1.9m); FY26 EBITDA guidance (~$3m) is now below FY25's $3.5m despite the capital raise and cost base being largely unchanged

Net bank debt fell to $5.1m at 30-Jun-2026 (from $8.2m at 31-Dec-2025) as capital-raise proceeds were first applied to debt paydown and settling extended supplier payment terms; interest-bearing bank debt was still $8.7m at 30-Jun-2026, and the business remains dependent on continued bank trade-finance support while it pursues an accelerated growth plan with a cut revenue outlook

financial.risk: Shareholder dilution already executed, growth plan funding shortfall
financial.description: May 2026 placement (to Wairahi Investments, $4.6m) plus a 1-for-7 rights issue (both at NZ$0.07/share) raised $8.9m combined against a $15m target for the accelerated growth path; shares outstanding have grown to roughly 562.6m; the funding shortfall implies either a scaled-back growth path or risk of a further raise, especially with FY26 trading now well below the plan's assumed starting point

Functional currency is largely USD-linked but presentation currency is NZD; NZD/USD movements affect reported revenue and profit, and FY26 guidance assumptions embed an FX rate that management has flagged as a swing factor

regulatory.description: April 2025 US reciprocal tariffs cost AoFrio its largest USA motor customer and have since also prompted other motor customers to shift to cheaper, lower-spec alternatives; this remains the single largest realized risk event in the company's recent history with no sign of resolution or like-for-like replacement business as of 3Q26
Reliance on a Vietnam-based contract manufacturer (East West) for motor production creates ongoing exposure to further shifts in US trade policy toward Vietnam-origin goods
Changing regulatory standards (e.g., US DOE water heater efficiency standards) can be a tailwind (driving ECR2 motor adoption) but also a compliance cost and uncertainty factor

macro.description: US tariff policy caused subdued customer capital spending through 2025 and has now directly cost the company its largest customer plus broader share loss across the motor customer base in 2026; management has twice lowered FY26 guidance as a result

Bottler/OEM capital purchase cycles are discretionary and can be deferred in a weaker macro environment, directly affecting AoFrio's hardware sell-through; management itself flags Q4 bottler/OEM budget timing as a forecasting risk

Net bank debt reduction in 1H26 (to $5.1m) has lessened near-term sensitivity versus year-end 2025, but the company remains reliant on bank trade-finance facilities to fund working capital and growth investment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Commercial refrigeration / cold drink equipment is a mature, essential replacement-and-growth market with a structural shift toward energy-efficient EC motor technology and IoT-enabled fleet management, reinforced by ESG/carbon-reduction targets among major beverage brands (refrigeration is ~35% of a cold drink's carbon footprint per company disclosure) and rising enterprise demand for connected asset management and AI-driven insights; however, the Motors sub-segment is now visibly exposed to US trade-policy shocks that can remove large customers abruptly and push the remaining customer base toward cheaper, lower-spec alternatives
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - revenue tied to customer capital expenditure cycles (bottler/OEM cooler fleet renewal and expansion) which can be deferred in weaker macro conditions or amid trade-policy uncertainty, as evidenced by the FY26 downturn triggered by tariff-driven customer reshoring and subsequent lower-spec motor substitution
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - continued (if reduced) use of bank trade finance and borrowings to fund working capital and growth investment means finance costs remain sensitive to base rates and facility utilization
key_input_costs: Electronic components and motor/fan raw materials (contract-manufactured in Vietnam)
Ocean freight/shipping (longer shipping times cited as a working capital driver)
Cloud/software engineering and R&D talent costs

recent_developments.event: FY2025 annual results released: record revenue of NZ$83.2m (+4.4%), EBITDA $3.5m (+$1.0m), gross margin 31.7% (+2.6pp), but revenue came in below the September 2025 updated guidance of ~$86m due to Q4-25 US tariff-driven motor demand weakness

1Q26 trading update: revenue $17.2m, down 28.1% YoY, as Motor revenue fell 52.9% to $5.7m following the loss of the largest US motor customer to tariff-driven onshoring; EBITDA -$0.4m (vs +$1.5m 1Q25); Chair John Scott described it as the company's first quarterly 'blip', expecting recovery in subsequent quarters

Placement of 65,134,806 shares to Wairahi Investments Limited at NZ$0.07/share raising NZ$4.559m, followed by a 1-for-7 pro-rata renounceable rights issue at NZ$0.07/share; combined raise totalled $8.9m against a $15m target for the accelerated growth path
Commercial launch of SCS 800 cellular controller and the general-release AoFrio iQ SaaS platform completed

1H26 interim result (6 months to 30-Jun-2026): revenue $33.8m, down 21.5% YoY, entirely attributable to the 50.5% (-$10.8m) Motors revenue decline; IoT revenue grew 6.8% to $23.2m; gross margin improved to 34.9% (from 29.6%) on mix shift; EBITDA $0.9m (aided by a $1.2m one-off 2025 RDTI tax credit); net bank debt fell to $5.1m (from $8.2m at FY25 year-end) as raise proceeds were applied to debt paydown; management said 'the improvement in full-year revenue now appears unlikely' for FY26
'Ask iQ', an AI-enabled fleet-insights feature, launched on the AoFrio iQ platform

3Q26 market update (9 months to 30-Sep-2026): revenue $50.3m, down 20% YoY; Motors revenue down 43.7% to $16.5m as other motor customers (beyond the originally lost largest customer) also shifted to lower-cost, lower-spec motors; IoT revenue roughly flat at $33.8m; 9M EBITDA $0.8m vs $2.7m prior year; FY26 guidance lowered again to revenue of ~$73m (~$10m below FY25) and EBITDA of ~$3m; AoFrio received its first SCS 800/AoFrio iQ purchase orders from major US bottlers; Chair John Scott: 'AoFrio is a business in transition, as reflected in the year-to-date results'
Company marked its 40th year in business (founded 1986 as Wellington Drive Technologies) with an announcement citing 3.7 million coolers now connected to the AoFrio cloud

Implied 4Q26 revenue is ~$22.7m
Below both the original FY26 'improvement' expectation and the Aug-2026 '$3.5m, broadly consistent with FY25' guide; implied 4Q26 EBITDA is ~$2.2m

items.target: Lower-cost componentry for the existing motor plus a new lower-cost motor model
items.notes: Response to broader customer shift toward lower-specification, lower-cost motors observed in 2Q/3Q26, not just the originally lost largest customer

items.target: Two-path FY26-FY30 framework: ~10% CAGR self-funded to $140m FY30 revenue/$14m EBITDA, or an externally funded 'aspirational' path targeting $300m FY30 revenue/$50m EBITDA

guidance.management_commentary: Chair John Scott described 1Q26 as the company's first quarterly 'blip' after a run of predictable, reliable results, attributing it to the loss of the largest US motor customer to tariffs and expressing confidence in recovery. By the 1H26 interim result, management tempered this to say full-year revenue improvement over FY25 'now appears unlikely'. By the 3Q26 update (29-Oct-2026), guidance was cut further to revenue of ~$73m and EBITDA of ~$3m, with management explicitly framing the broader cause as other motor customers -- not just the one originally lost -- shifting to lower-cost, lower-specification products. Scott summarized the period as 'AoFrio is a business in transition, as reflected in the year-to-date results,' while pointing to the first SCS 800/AoFrio iQ purchase orders from major US bottlers and the new 'Ask iQ' feature as evidence the SaaS transition is beginning to gain commercial traction, with cellular revenue expected to rise significantly in 2027.

bull_case: First commercial purchase orders for SCS 800 and AoFrio iQ have now been won from major US bottlers (3Q26), the clearest evidence to date that the hardware-to-SaaS pivot can convert trials into revenue, with management guiding to significantly higher cellular revenue in 2027

IoT segment has held up through the Motors downturn (9M26 revenue roughly flat at $33.8m versus FY25's +8.9% growth) and now represents roughly two-thirds of group revenue at materially better gross margins (34.4% blended 9M26, 40.9% IoT-specific) than the legacy Motors business, continuing to validate the mix-shift thesis

Balance sheet has de-levered: net bank debt fell to $5.1m at 30-Jun-2026 from $8.2m at year-end 2025 as capital-raise proceeds were applied to debt paydown first, improving capacity to self-fund the next phase of growth investment without an immediate further raise

Diversification into Food Retail (70-store Latin American supermarket rollout progressing, with the customer discussing additional stores) and a new AI-enabled 'Ask iQ' feature (Oct-2026) reduce long-term dependence on the volatile CDE/Motors business and support the recurring-revenue ambition

Deep, 40-year OEM/bottler relationships, a large (3.68m device) connected installed base, and high customer satisfaction (NPS +62 in FY25) provide a durable, hard-to-replicate distribution channel for the SaaS products as they scale
bear_case: FY26 guidance has now been cut twice within the year -- from an expected improvement over FY25's record $83.2m, to 'broadly consistent' EBITDA in August, to a ~12% revenue decline (~$73m) and lower EBITDA (~$3m) by the October 3Q26 update -- indicating persistently poor earnings visibility

The customer-concentration problem has broadened rather than resolved: beyond the originally lost largest US motor customer, other motor customers shifted to lower-cost, lower-specification products in 2Q/3Q26, driving a 43.7% nine-month Motors revenue decline and showing the pressure is structural to the segment, not a one-off event

Core recurring/cellular revenue remains small (roughly 6% of 9M26 group revenue) despite years of strategic emphasis and a long-stated 50% target; monetizing the newly won 3Q26 purchase orders at scale in 2027 is unproven and execution-dependent

Meaningful shareholder dilution has already occurred (May-June 2026 placement and 1-for-7 rights issue, both at NZ$0.07/share, well below prior trading levels and above the current ~NZ$0.05 share price), raising shares outstanding to ~562.6m, and the raise still fell short of its $15m target for the preferred growth path, leaving open the risk of further dilution

The stock has materially de-rated through 2026 (from a 52-week high near NZ$0.11 to around NZ$0.05, market cap near NZ$30m) alongside the repeated guidance cuts, and the company continues to post statutory losses (1H26 loss $2.1m) even with EBITDA positive, aided by non-recurring items such as the FY25 RDTI tax credit
